{{Short description|Special triangle based on arbitrary triangle}}
[[File:Fuhrmann triangle.svg|thumb|upright=1.5|Fuhrmann triangle (red): <math>\triangle M^\prime_c M^\prime_b M^\prime_a </math> <br/> mid arc points: <math>M_a, M_b, M_c </math>]]
[[File:Fuhrmann triangle2.svg|thumb|upright=1.5|Fuhrmann triangle (red): <math>\triangle M^\prime_c M^\prime_b M^\prime_a </math> <br/>  <math>\triangle M^\prime_c M^\prime_b M^\prime_a  \sim \triangle M_a M_b M_c </math>]]
The '''Fuhrmann triangle''', named after [[Wilhelm Fuhrmann]] (1833–1904), is special triangle based on a given arbitrary triangle.

For a given triangle <math>\triangle ABC</math> and its [[circumcircle]] the midpoints of the arcs over triangle sides are denoted by  <math>M_a, M_b, M_c </math>. Those midpoints get reflected at the associated triangle sides yielding the points <math>M^\prime_a, M^\prime_b, M^\prime_c </math>, which forms the ''Fuhrmann triangle''.<ref name="raj"> Roger A. Johnson: ''Advanced Euclidean Geometry''. Dover 2007, {{ISBN|978-0-486-46237-0}}, pp.&nbsp;228–229,&nbsp;300 (originally published 1929 with Houghton Mifflin Company (Boston) as ''Modern Geometry'').</ref><ref>Ross Honsberger: ''Episodes in Nineteenth and Twentieth Century Euclidean Geometry''. MAA, 1995, pp. [https://books.google.com/books?id=7vcrmWEV73AC&pg=PA49 49-52] </ref>

The circumcircle of Fuhrmann triangle is the [[Fuhrmann circle]]. Furthermore the Furhmann triangle is similar to the triangle formed by the mid arc points, that is <math>\triangle M^\prime_c M^\prime_b M^\prime_a  \sim \triangle M_a M_b M_c </math>.<ref name="raj"/> For the area of the Fuhrmann triangle the following formula holds:<ref name="mw"> {{MathWorld|title=Fuhrmann triangle|urlname=FuhrmannTriangle}} (retrieved 2019-11-12)</ref>

:<math>|\triangle M^\prime_c M^\prime_b M^\prime_a| = \frac{(a+b+c)|OI|^2}{4R}=\frac{(a+b+c)(R-2r)}{4}</math>

Where <math>O</math> denotes the circumcenter of the given triangle <math>\triangle ABC</math> and  <math>R</math> its radius as well as <math>I</math> denoting the incenter and <math>r</math> its radius. Due to [[Euler's theorem in geometry|Euler's theorem]] one also has  <math>|OI|^2=R(R-2r)</math>. The following equations hold for the sides of the Fuhrmann triangle:<ref name="mw"/>

:<math>a^\prime=\sqrt{\frac{(-a+b+c)(a+b+c)}{bc}}|OI|</math>
:<math>b^\prime=\sqrt{\frac{(a-b+c)(a+b+c)}{ac}}|OI|</math>
:<math>c^\prime=\sqrt{\frac{(a+b-c)(a+b+c)}{ab}}|OI|</math>

Where <math>a, b, c</math> denote the sides of the given triangle <math>\triangle ABC</math> and <math>a^\prime, b^\prime, c^\prime</math> the sides of the Fuhrmann triangle (see drawing).
